mcq.question: Why can `RoastBatch::is_known_bean` be called without any `RoastBatch` object?

options.A: It is a static member function, so it has no `this` pointer and belongs to the class
options.C: It is defined inside the class body

mcq.explanation: Static member functions are called as `RoastBatch::is_known_bean(...)`. They cannot access non-static members because there is no object.

mcq.question: What must `add_beans` return for `batch.add_beans(500).set_roast(Roast::dark)` to modify `batch` itself?
mcq.explanation: Returning a non-const reference lets the next call act on the same object. Returning by value would chain on a temporary copy, and const would forbid the mutator.

bonus.question: Static data such as a global batch counter is shared by every object and every thread. What problems could appear if two threads create batches at the same time, and how would you fix them?
Write a failing test for `RoastBatch::heaviest(const std::vector<RoastBatch>&)`, a static function returning the batch with the most green beans, then implement it.
